title: Iteration 1 — chasing clarity
summary: Started testing a lighter morning cup with spice layered into the brew instead of sweetness. The cup felt flat overall but surprisingly clean.
observation: Woke up after decent sleep and entered the session slightly tired but mentally stable. The aroma leaned heavily toward spice before the first sip and the coffee itself stayed in the background. Texture felt thinner than expected. Alertness improved after the cup but energy stayed physical low. The interesting part was the emotional shift — I felt more willing to sit down and work even though my body still felt sleepy.
field_note: The cup didn’t feel exciting yet, but it made work feel easier to begin.

title: Iteration 2 — spice took over
summary: Introduced a stronger spice direction to test freshness and lift. The brew became much more expressive but also lost balance.
observation: The aroma immediately resembled spiced tea before even tasting like coffee. Spice dominated the top half of the cup while the coffee appeared later in the sip. Mood uplift was noticeably stronger than the previous session and focus improved quickly. Physically though, there was still a sleepy layer underneath. By the bottom of the cup the spice residue became too present and overpowered the finish completely.
field_note: The drink became memorable today, but not necessarily balanced.

title: Iteration 3 — too comforting
summary: Tried layering warmth into the morning profile. The result became more comforting than energising.
observation: The cup smelled warm and inviting but the spice blend softened the coffee too much. The body became pleasant with breakfast but mentally the effect drifted toward calm instead of sharpness. Focus uplift was weaker compared to previous sessions. This was the first moment where I realised some ingredients emotionally slow the drink down even if the caffeine remains the same.
field_note: Not every warm cup creates momentum.

title: Iteration 4 — closer to balance
summary: Freshly prepared the spice element differently today and the balance improved noticeably.
observation: The top half of the cup finally felt cleaner. Aroma still entered before the coffee but no longer interrupted the experience completely. Coffee started showing up in the middle of the sip rather than disappearing entirely. I still noticed spice residue settling toward the bottom of the cup which changed the finish again. Physically I remained slightly sleepy after the cup, but mentally I became alert enough to immediately want to work. The emotional shift was clearer than the physical shift.
field_note: This was the first version that felt directionally right instead of merely interesting.

title: Iteration 1 — too medicinal
summary: The first evening-style experiment became heavier and more medicinal than intended.
observation: Served this to family during a rushed evening. The cup felt dense, thick and strongly spiced. One person compared it to a traditional herbal drink rather than coffee. The texture was interesting but the flavour balance leaned bitter and overwhelming. Socially, it slowed people down but not in a pleasant café way. More in a ‘what exactly is this?’ kind of way.
field_note: The line between ritual and medicinal is thinner than I expected.

title: Iteration 2 — mocha territory
summary: Reduced the harshness and moved closer toward a café-style conversational drink.
observation: The texture became smoother and easier to drink. The aroma shifted away from harsh spice into something closer to dark chocolate and café mocha. Personally this became the first evening cup I genuinely enjoyed slowly. It naturally reduced drinking speed and made the session feel heavier in a comforting way. Family feedback also improved and people acknowledged the progression from the previous version.
field_note: This was the first cup that felt like it belonged beside conversation instead of analysis.

title: Iteration 3 — too close to kahwa
summary: Experimented with a cleaner infusion approach but the cup lost its emotional identity.
observation: The drink visually and aromatically started resembling spiced herbal tea more than coffee. Family immediately guessed spice before coffee. The cup lost some of its comforting density while bitterness stayed. The emotional response also changed — instead of encouraging conversation, it became something I analysed while drinking. This version revealed that simplifying ingredients alone does not automatically improve emotional clarity.
field_note: Removing noise also removed some soul.
